html:
Gateway Local AI runtimes

Local AI Runtimes is an optional skill for inspecting and managing model servers on the selected Gateway. It starts disabled. Enable it through the ordinary capability controls; existing permissions, confirmations and target selection still apply. Its operations inspect metadata and manage processes/model storage without making helper inference calls.

The controller's Inference area has its own installation, build and instance workflows. This Gateway skill uses accepted Parameter profiles and already available provider executables. Starting a Gateway runtime does not change Main or Helper. Explicit activation can change Main for future work through the same revisioned owner as Model Configuration.

Prepare a profile

  1. Select the Gateway that will own the provider. It must advertise local_ai_runtime, controlled by GATEWAY_ENABLE_LLM_RUNTIME. The setting defaults to enabled on Linux and disabled on other platforms when unspecified. The process adapters reject managed startup on Windows.
  2. Use the Local AI Runtime template in Parameter Store. Set the Gateway's logical node ID, provider, host and port. Managed vLLM needs an existing absolute local model path; llama.cpp needs an existing absolute model file. The optional working directory must be an existing absolute directory.
  3. If authentication is needed, store it separately with the Local AI API key template and set the runtime profile's api_key_ref. Accept both Parameter references for the task. Profiles and keys are resolved from accepted bindings; an unaccepted current Parameter value is not substituted later.
  4. Inspect local_ai.profiles for the accepted profile revision, and local_ai.status for provider discovery. Start with the profile reference and that revision. A stale revision fails instead of changing the requested launch.

Profiles are closed, typed objects. They accept an IP-literal host, a bounded port, provider-specific options and an optional controller-reachable URL. They do not accept an arbitrary shell command. Defaults are loopback 127.0.0.1, port 8000, API root /v1, startup timeout 60 seconds, health timeout three seconds and a 1 MiB log ring. Startup timeout accepts 1–300 seconds; health timeout accepts 1–10. Choose the actual provider port explicitly when its existing server uses another port. An external-only compatible profile can use a different API root.

An external bind requires all three: external_bind_confirmed in the profile, GATEWAY_LOCAL_AI_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_BIND on the Gateway, and a nonempty API key. Ordinary unsafe-action/confirmation policy also applies. Wildcard hosts count as external. These checks control startup; they do not create a firewall rule or TLS listener. The profile's local probe origin uses HTTP, mapping wildcard binds to loopback. A separate controller_base_url may use HTTP or HTTPS.

Provider behavior

Provider Supported behavior and limits
vllm Probe the known executable, construct a validated launch plan for an existing model path, inspect health/models and bounded metrics. Requested flags must appear in installed help.
llamacpp Use llama-server, an existing model file and advertised offline support. Inspect health/models and metrics when the server provides them.
ollama Manage ollama serve; inspect served, installed and loaded model metadata. Pull and remove are explicit separate mutations. A managed launch with a nonempty key is rejected, so external managed binding is unavailable through this adapter.
lmstudio Inspect health/model inventory. Discovering lms does not grant managed start/stop/restart.
generic_openai_compatible Inspect an externally managed endpoint's model inventory/health. No process lifecycle, detailed model metadata or metrics adapter is supplied.

The adapters inspect executable help with a bounded read and timeout. Launch plans use an allowlisted environment and explicit argument vectors, without a shell. vLLM/llama.cpp launches use offline model behavior; Ollama model downloads require pull_model. Keys use supported environment variables rather than command-line arguments. A successful metadata probe establishes only that observation; it does not certify generation, tool-calling or tokenizer behavior.

Ollama pulls have a five-minute observation budget and bounded streamed records. Only the success record confirms download. Cancellation or a lost stream can leave the provider's effect unknown. Inspect installed models before deciding what to do next. Removing a model is a separate confirmed write.

Request ownership

flowchart LR Task[Accepted task and Parameter bindings] --> Skill[Local AI tool/service] Skill --> Profiles[Accepted profile and private key resolution] Profiles --> Client[Selected-Gateway client] Client --> Gateway[Authenticated inbound or outbound Gateway] Gateway --> Manager[Runtime manager and effect journal] Manager --> Adapter[Provider adapter] Adapter --> Provider[Owned process or external metadata endpoint] Skill --> Activation[Explicit controller activation] Activation --> Routing[Revisioned Main model routing]
Implementation owner Responsibility
Skill and tool definitions Availability, closed arguments, effect/confirmation metadata, resource claims and cancellation transport.
Accepted profiles Resolve pinned Parameter values and private secret references; expose a secret-free profile inventory.
Controller service Keep profile inventory/activation local and dispatch provider operations once to the selected Gateway.
Gateway client Bind node and execution identity, use authenticated inbound/outbound transport, bound responses and preserve uncertain effects.
Contracts and receipt validation Validate profiles/operations, resource claims and bounded success/failure envelopes.
Runtime manager Own processes, admission, cancellation, public runtime records and mutation replay.
Provider adapters and HTTP reader Validate executable capabilities, construct launch plans and read bounded provider metadata.
Activation service Preview, apply, reconcile and restore Main endpoint changes through canonical model routing.

The Gateway exposes /local-ai/operation and /local-ai/cancel. It checks the request's node before dispatch. Profile inventory and controller activation do not go through the Gateway manager. Read availability does not grant mutation permission. Heavy startup/download/deletion work additionally uses local GPU-family admission; the Agent scheduler owns cross-skill resource dimensions. GPU configuration and startup share coordination described in GPU ownership.

Lifecycle, logs and recovery

The manager records mutation identity and an unknown-outcome fence before dispatch. The digest binds operation, arguments and profile revision. Repeating the same execution ID returns its retained receipt; changing its intent is rejected. The manager retains at most 1,024 mutation receipts and 256 runtime rows. Capacity failure does not discard uncertain effects to make them replayable.

Before spawn, the manager checks profile identity, resource/restart state, exposure policy, provider capability, working directory and port availability. It persists runtime intent before creating the process session, closing the crash-before-PID-record window. It then retains the process handle, accepted profile/key and a bounded log buffer in memory. Startup waits for health within the profile timeout. A timeout can leave the process starting; inspect runtime, health and logs before another lifecycle action.

Stop requires a process owned by the current manager and uses the recorded process group identity. It never selects a process by port. Restart stops that owned runtime and uses its originally accepted profile, model, port and credentials. Cancellation signals a pending operation or records a pre-dispatch fence; its acknowledgement does not by itself prove that a provider-side effect stopped.

The node-specific manifest is under <artifact_root>/local_ai/<node-name-hash>/runtimes.json. Saves write a private temporary file, flush/fsync it and replace the prior manifest. Public runtime observations and operation receipts survive; process handles, profile/key objects and log buffers do not. After Gateway replacement, retained PIDs have unknown ownership. Process evidence can establish exit, but the new manager does not adopt or kill an old PID. Unknown ownership blocks automatic relaunch of the same profile. Resolve the existing process through the operator's process/service owner instead of deleting the effect record or repeating a start blindly.

Logs use offsets into the transformed, bounded UTF-8 stream. The known API key is masked before storage, with additional catalog text sanitization. Overlong lines are omitted as a whole. Eviction advances the retained base offset; a stale offset returns truncation evidence. Logs are available only while this manager retains their buffer. Metrics expose bounded finite name/value pairs and omit labels.

Explicit Main endpoint activation

activation_preview requires the accepted profile reference/revision and model ID. For a remote Gateway, provide a controller-reachable controller_base_url; Gateway loopback is not controller loopback. The accepted profile key must agree with the canonical Main credential. Activation does not silently move an existing credential to a newly selected endpoint.

The preview reads model inventory from both controller and Gateway viewpoints and requires the same sorted IDs, including the requested model. It records the candidate, previous endpoint/model, routing revision and rollback facts for ten minutes. Preview records are bounded to 256 retained records. This is metadata-only compatibility checking and does not generate a completion.

activate_for_smto rechecks the candidate and current configuration, records an applying state, then updates Main through revisioned routing while preserving its generation settings. Repeated calls reconcile only the exact expected revision. restore_smto_endpoint likewise restores the recorded endpoint/model only when the intervening configuration still matches. A later edit—even one that returns to the same values—can invalidate a preview or restore. Create a new preview instead of overwriting that edit. Accepted tasks keep their captured configuration; future work uses the changed Main endpoint. Helper is not assigned by this workflow.

Validation and operational limits

Contract tests exercise closed profiles, fake-provider lifecycle, revision/replay fences, logs, cancellation and isolated process-group cleanup. Integration fixtures exercise accepted Parameters, model-routing activation, both Gateway transports, bounded local HTTP metadata and canonical receipts. These checks need no installed provider or GPU and perform no model download or generation. They do not establish compatibility for a particular deployed provider/version/model combination.
